Trypsin: Named in 1876 by German physiologist Wilhelm Kühne (from Greek 'thrýpto' – 'I break'); obtained from bovine or porcine pancreas. First approval/introduction: Pharmaceutical use of pancreatic proteases since the mid-20th century. Bromelain: Extracted commercially from pineapple stems (Thailand, Malaysia); heat-labile (≈83% activity remains after 1 h at 50 °C). First approval/introduction: EMA 2012: bromelain-based topical product approved for debridement of severe burns. Rutoside Trihydrate (Rutin): Found in buckwheat, citrus, Ruta graveolens and asparagus; under research for venous insufficiency and post-thrombotic syndrome. First approval/introduction: Used as a vasoprotective in Europe since the mid-20th century. Aceclofenac: A glycolic acid ester of diclofenac developed in Spain; widely used in Europe and India for osteoarthritis, RA and ankylosing spondylitis. First approval/introduction: Patented 1983; approved 1992 (Prodesfarma / Almirall, Spain).
Trypsin 48 mg + Bromelain 90 mg + Rutoside trihydrate 100 mg + Aceclofenac 100
Adds NSAID analgesia (aceclofenac) to the anti-oedematous action of proteolytic enzymes and bioflavonoid.

Trypsin Serine protease that hydrolyses proteins in inflammatory exudate and fibrin deposits, reducing oedema and accelerating resolution of inflammation and haematoma. Receptor / target profile: Cleaves peptide bonds on the carboxyl side of lysine and arginine; degrades fibrin and inflammatory debris.

Bromelain Cysteine protease mixture that modulates inflammatory mediators (bradykinin, prostaglandins), reduces oedema, has fibrinolytic and anti-platelet effects. Receptor / target profile: Sulfhydryl proteases that modulate bradykinin and prostaglandin pathways, reduce oedema, and have fibrinolytic and antiplatelet effects.

Rutoside Trihydrate (Rutin) Reduces capillary permeability and fragility, scavenges free radicals and inhibits inflammatory mediators, complementing proteolytic enzymes in reducing oedema. Receptor / target profile: Reduces capillary permeability and fragility; antioxidant; inhibits platelet aggregation and inflammatory mediators.

Aceclofenac Inhibits cyclo-oxygenase (preferential COX-2) reducing prostaglandin synthesis; also inhibits IL-1 and TNF and stimulates cartilage matrix synthesis. Analgesic, anti-inflammatory and antipyretic. Receptor / target profile: Inhibits COX (preferential COX-2) and suppresses IL-1beta and TNF; stimulates glycosaminoglycan synthesis in cartilage.

Summary: Partially absorbed intact from the gut.

Summary: Partly absorbed; hydrolysed by gut flora to quercetin.
Hepatic – CYP2C9 to 4'-hydroxyaceclofenac (main), small amounts of diclofenac
Summary: Rapid, complete absorption; Tmax 1.25–3 h. >99% protein bound. Metabolised to 4'-hydroxyaceclofenac and diclofenac (CYP2C9). Half-life ~4 h.

Bromelain: Take on an empty stomach.
Rutoside Trihydrate (Rutin): With or without food.
Aceclofenac: Take after food or with milk; avoid alcohol (GI bleeding).
Aceclofenac: BP, renal function, LFTs and CBC on prolonged use; signs of GI bleeding.

Trypsin: Supportive care. Bromelain: Supportive care. Rutoside Trihydrate (Rutin): Supportive care. Aceclofenac: Nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, GI bleeding, renal failure, convulsions (rare). Supportive care; activated charcoal.
Inform if allergic to pineapple, papaya or latex
Do not combine with other painkillers containing NSAIDs
Report black stools, vomiting blood, chest pain, swelling
Use for the shortest time needed
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
